help.intro: A short text of about 130 words about the countries where German is spoken: Germany, Austria, Switzerland and little Liechtenstein, plus a surprise about Switzerland, which has four national languages and no language called Swiss. All facts are real and were checked. You need what you have just learnt: country names (most without article, but die Schweiz), the verbs sprechen, wohnen, kommen aus and liegen, and the languages Deutsch, Französisch, Italienisch. Read for the gist first, then answer each question from one sentence.
help.tips[0].title: Countries with and without an article
help.tips[0].text: Most countries have no article: Deutschland, Österreich, Liechtenstein, Frankreich, Italien. A few are feminine and take die: die Schweiz, die Türkei, die Ukraine. After aus and in, die becomes der: aus der Schweiz, in der Schweiz; but aus Österreich, in Österreich. The language is usually the country word with -isch: Französisch, Italienisch; Deutsch has no -isch.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Lukas comes from Switzerland and now lives in Austria.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: In Liechtenstein people speak German, in Geneva French.
help.tips[0].check.why: Schweiz takes die; after aus it becomes der.
help.tips[1].text: In der Schweiz spricht man vier Sprachen: man means people, one, you in general. It takes the er/sie/es form of the verb: man spricht, man sagt, man wohnt. Very common in texts about countries and customs.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: In Austria people say Grüß Gott, in Hamburg people say Moin.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: How do you say thank you in French? Merci.
help.tips[1].check.q: In der Schweiz ____ man Deutsch, Französisch, Italienisch und Rätoromanisch.
help.tips[1].check.why: man takes the er/sie/es form: man spricht.
help.remember[0]: die Schweiz: aus der Schweiz, in der Schweiz; other countries without article.
help.remember[1]: man spricht / man sagt = people speak / people say.
help.exam: Short factual texts about countries and languages with multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: Four countries speak German, and one of them has four languages but no language of its own. Read which, and who is the smallest.
passageTranslation:
German is spoken in four countries in Europe: in Germany, in Austria, in Switzerland and in Liechtenstein.

Germany is big. About eighty-four million people live here. The capital is Berlin. Austria is smaller. About nine million people live there. The capital is Vienna.

Switzerland is special. It has four languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. About sixty per cent speak German. In Geneva people speak French, in Lugano Italian. A language called 'Swiss' does not exist! The capital is Bern, but the biggest city is Zurich.

Liechtenstein is very small. It lies between Switzerland and Austria. Only forty thousand people live there. The country has no airport and no motorway. The capital is called Vaduz.

In Basel there is a special place: the three-country corner. Here Germany, France and Switzerland meet. You stand in one country and see two others.
questions[0].explanation: "Deutsch spricht man in vier Ländern in Europa."
questions[0].questionTranslation: In how many countries is German spoken?
questions[1].explanation: "Österreich ist kleiner. Dort wohnen etwa neun Millionen Menschen."
questions[1].questionTranslation: How many people live in Austria?
questions[2].explanation: "In Genf spricht man Französisch, in Lugano Italienisch."
questions[2].questionTranslation: Which language is spoken in Lugano?
questions[3].explanation: "Eine Sprache ‚Schweizerisch‘ gibt es nicht!" The four languages are German, French, Italian and Romansh.
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: Yes, sixty per cent speak Swiss.
questions[3].optionsTranslation[2]: No, Switzerland has four other languages.
questions[4].explanation: "Die Hauptstadt ist Bern, aber die größte Stadt ist Zürich."
questions[4].questionTranslation: What is the capital of Switzerland?
questions[5].explanation: "Es liegt zwischen der Schweiz und Österreich."
questions[6].explanation: "Das Land hat keinen Flughafen und keine Autobahn."
questions[7].explanation: "Hier treffen sich Deutschland, Frankreich und die Schweiz."
questions[7].questionTranslation: Which three countries meet at the three-country corner in Basel?
help.tips[1].title: man = people in general
